descriptionChirho: To arrange troops in battle formation or array an army for war (Qal with military context; Arabic cognate صَفَّ / اصْطَفَّ 'form ranks', Swahili -panga vita, Korean 전열을 갖추다 / 진을 치다).

To set things in proper order or arrangement, especially wood on an altar, showbread on a table, or a legal case before God (Qal general/cultic sense; Arabic رَتَّبَ 'put in order', Swahili -panga, Korean 정돈하다 / 배열하다).

To prepare or make ready, especially a table or provision (Qal with preparatory nuance; Arabic أَعَدَّ / مُعَدَّةٌ 'prepare/prepared', Swahili -andaa / -tayarisha 'make ready', Korean 준비하다 / 차리다 'prepare/set a table').
To be comparable to, match, or equal in value (Qal figurative sense; Arabic عادَلَ 'equal' / قارَنَ 'compare', Swahili -linganisha 'compare', Korean 비교하다 'compare').
